references.text: The introduction to the laws concerning a discharge from a man's body, which verse 3 elaborates on further
Describes the purification after the discharge has stopped, which is the result of the condition described in verse 3
Refers to the zav (discharge) as a state that makes priests unclean and prevents them from eating the holy offerings
Commands that anyone with a discharge must be sent outside the camp to preserve the camp's purity
David's curse on Joab's house includes that there should always be someone with a discharge (zav) - the same condition described in Leviticus 15:3
